r0.why: Deposit of a turbidity current distributing vast clastic sediment to the deep ocean (1); density flow, not tractional or frictional (13).

r1.why: Frictional drag called tractional flow (14), required velocity to suspend and push (15), larger or denser particle needs higher velocity (16).

r2.why: Liquefaction changing fluid density (17), turbulent liquid with fine suspended load forming slurry (18), lower density contrast lets larger fragments move at low velocity (19).

r3.why: Bouma 1962 first proper description and fining-up intervals (2,3), the anomaly (4), cycle from erosional conglomerate base to siltstone and shale (5), strong to waning flow (6), complete cycle rare due to erosion (7).

r4.why: Bouma applies to low-density currents (9), dispersive pressures hinder settling (10), different structures as a consequence (11), Lowe sequence complements Bouma (12).

r5.why: Condition occurs beyond deep ocean where turbidites are well represented (20); lahars, mudslides, pyroclastic flows, the latter especially similar (21).

r6.why: Lake and fjord turbidites dating landslides and presumed earthquakes by radiocarbon or varves (38), lode gold at Bendigo and Ballarat over 2,600 tons (39), lithified accumulations as hydrocarbon reservoirs (41).
